note: 編む directly includes plaiting or braiding, and the strand and hair context selects that sense over knitting.
クォーター is the ordinary Japanese name for the US or Canadian 25-cent coin; the definition supplies the country and value context.
パイナップル and thơm both name the pineapple plant; thơm is a standard southern Vietnamese regional term, with dứa common in the north.
エピデミック is a direct Japanese equivalent for epidemic, and dịch is the natural Vietnamese noun for an outbreak of disease.
情報源 means a source of information generally. 情報提供者 is glossed as informant or contact in JMdict (ent_seq 2366020 sense 0), matching a reporter's source.
Dấu âm normally names a negative sign. Dấu trừ is the standard Vietnamese term for the minus symbol used for subtraction and for a negative number.
急行列車 explicitly means express train. 急行 is the shorter Japanese express service term and is glossed as express train in JMdict (ent_seq 1228690 sense 1).
トマト and cà chua commonly name both the tomato fruit and plant, so the plant sense is clear in this context.
Lượt nhấp chuột is understandable but emphasizes a counted turn or occurrence. Cú nhấp chuột is the more common Vietnamese expression for one mouse-click action.
Pháo đài can suggest an artillery fort. Thành trì is a broader Vietnamese term for a fortified stronghold, matching the English definition.
Mô ten is an unnatural phonetic spelling. Khách sạn ven đường clearly describes the roadside lodging with convenient automobile access in this definition.
写本 is usually a handwritten copy of an existing book. 手稿 is glossed as manuscript in JMdict (ent_seq 2779790 sense 0) and better covers an original handwritten or manually typed work.
工匠 is archaic, and nghệ nhân often suggests a master artist. 職人 means craftsman or artisan in JMdict (ent_seq 1357550 sense 0), while thợ thủ công is a general skilled craft worker.
Lọ is ambiguous and usually means a jar. Bồ hóng is the common Vietnamese word for soot particles from incomplete combustion.
Vở is a notebook generally. Vở bài tập specifies a student booklet containing exercises or problems and space for answers.
Chủng is valid but uncommon as a standalone verb. Tiêm chủng is the standard Vietnamese verb phrase for administering a vaccine to produce immunity.
Người vay usually means a borrower of money. Người mượn covers someone borrowing an object or other thing generally.
Thích is a correct but technical or rare Vietnamese word for maple. Cây phong is the common natural equivalent for a maple tree.
アボカド and bơ are standard names for avocado; the fruit context distinguishes Vietnamese bơ from butter.
朝鮮人参 specifically names Asian ginseng Panax ginseng, while the English definition includes both Asian and American Panax species; no broader verified Japanese term was found offline.
Cần is a natural shortening but can be ambiguous. Cần câu is the complete Vietnamese term for a fishing rod.
Lò phản ứng can refer to chemical or other reactors. Lò phản ứng hạt nhân specifies a device using atomic energy to produce heat.
Tiện lợi means convenient generally. Thân thiện với người dùng specifically describes a design that is easy and intuitive for an untrained user.
つばを吐く is limited to saliva. 吐き出す means spit out in JMdict (ent_seq 1444140 sense 0), covering saliva or another substance from the mouth.
Lọ is a general jar or bottle. Lọ nhỏ captures the small-vessel sense of vial without limiting its contents to medicine.
反吐 is coarse in register. 嘔吐物 is the neutral medical or descriptive term for vomit or vomited matter in JMdict (ent_seq 2767050 sense 0).
ふじつぼ refers specifically to acorn barnacles. 蔓脚類 is glossed as Cirripedia or barnacles in JMdict (ent_seq 2831850 sense 0), matching the wider subclass definition.
Lưới means net generally. Lưới đánh cá specifies the net used for fishing.

おもしろおかしい and hài hước describe funny or humorous without the strong intensity. 抱腹絶倒 means laughing oneself into convulsions in JMdict (ent_seq 1603380 sense 0); cực kỳ buồn cười adds the required very funny force.
オウム is commonly limited to large parrots such as cockatoos, while the English definition includes the whole parrot order or Psittacidae; no single verified broader Japanese term was found.
触角 and râu both name the sensory appendage on insects or crustaceans; the animal context selects this sense of the Vietnamese word.
Ham muốn means desire generally. Ham muốn tình dục specifies the sexual arousal sense, while still allowing the broader strong-desire reading in context.
オーバーオール and quần yếm refer to bib overalls, narrower than the English definition of any protective garment worn over clothing; no verified general equivalent covers that wider sense.
Phá hoại is general damage or sabotage. Phá hoại tài sản specifies willful damage or destruction of property, including graffiti or defacement.
Báo thức usually refers to a wake-up alarm. Thiết bị báo động covers mechanical devices for waking people or drawing attention more generally.
Ốm varies by region and can mean sick. Gầy is the broadly understood Vietnamese adjective for thin, including a negative or underweight sense.
Hoan hô is a public cheer like hooray or bravo. Vui quá is a more personal informal exclamation of happiness like yay.
アミュレット is a less common loanword; お守り is the ordinary Japanese amulet in JMdict (ent_seq 1002060 sense 0). Bùa hộ mệnh specifies a protective Vietnamese charm, not a harmful spell.
きび specifically means proso millet, while the English definition covers multiple millet grasses and grains; no broader verified Japanese equivalent was found offline.
Keo can mean glue or hair gel generally. Sáp vuốt tóc specifies the greasy or waxy styling product described by pomade.
